12.L120:
<n>120:1</n> Levávi óculos meos in montes, * unde véniet auxílium mihi.
<n>120:2</n> Auxílium meum a Dómino, * qui fecit cælum et terram.
<n>120:3</n> Non det in commotiónem pedem tuum: * neque dormítet qui custódit te.
<n>120:4</n> Ecce, non dormitábit neque dórmiet, * qui custódit Israël.
<n>120:5</n> Dóminus custódit te, Dóminus protéctio tua, * super manum déxteram tuam.
<n>120:6</n> Per diem sol non uret te: * neque luna per noctem.
<n>120:7</n> Dóminus custódit te ab omni malo: * custódiat ánimam tuam Dóminus.
<n>120:8</n> Dóminus custódiat intróitum tuum, et éxitum tuum: * ex hoc nunc, et usque in sǽculum.
12.E120:
<n>120:1</n> I have lifted up my eyes to the mountains, * from whence help shall come to me.
<n>120:2</n> My help is from the Lord, * who made heaven and earth.
<n>120:3</n> May he not suffer thy foot to be moved: * neither let him slumber that keepeth thee.
<n>120:4</n> Behold he shall neither slumber nor sleep, * that keepeth Israel.
<n>120:5</n> The Lord is thy keeper, the Lord is thy protection * upon thy right hand.
<n>120:6</n> The sun shall not burn thee by day: * nor the moon by night.
<n>120:7</n> The Lord keepeth thee from all evil: * may the Lord keep thy soul.
<n>120:8</n> May the Lord keep thy coming in and thy going out; * from henceforth now and for ever.
12.L121:
<n>121:1</n> Lætátus sum in his, quæ dicta sunt mihi: * In domum Dómini íbimus.
<n>121:2</n> Stantes erant pedes nostri, * in átriis tuis, Jerúsalem.
<n>121:3</n> Jerúsalem, quæ ædificátur ut cívitas: * cujus participátio ejus in idípsum.
<n>121:4</n> Illuc enim ascendérunt tribus, tribus Dómini: * testimónium Israël ad confiténdum nómini Dómini.
<n>121:5</n> Quia illic sedérunt sedes in judício, * sedes super domum David.
<n>121:6</n> Rogáte quæ ad pacem sunt Jerúsalem: * et abundántia diligéntibus te:
<n>121:7</n> Fiat pax in virtúte tua: * et abundántia in túrribus tuis.
<n>121:8</n> Propter fratres meos, et próximos meos, * loquébar pacem de te:
<n>121:9</n> Propter domum Dómini, Dei nostri, * quæsívi bona tibi.
12.L122:
<n>122:1</n> Ad te levávi óculos meos, * qui hábitas in cælis.
<n>122:3</n> Miserére nostri, Dómine, miserére nostri: * quia multum repléti sumus despectióne:
<n>122:4</n> Quia multum repléta est ánima nostra: * oppróbrium abundántibus, et despéctio supérbis.
12.L123:
<n>123:1</n> Nisi quia Dóminus erat in nobis, dicat nunc Israël: * (2a) nisi quia Dóminus erat in nobis,
<n>123:5</n> Torréntem pertransívit ánima nostra: * fórsitan pertransísset ánima nostra aquam intolerábilem.
<n>123:6</n> Benedíctus Dóminus * qui non dedit nos in captiónem déntibus eórum.
<n>123:8</n> Adjutórium nostrum in nómine Dómini, * qui fecit cælum et terram.
12.L124:
<n>124:1</n> Qui confídunt in Dómino, sicut mons Sion: * non commovébitur in ætérnum, qui hábitat (2a) in Jerúsalem.
<n>124:3</n> Quia non relínquet Dóminus virgam peccatórum super sortem justórum: * ut non exténdant justi ad iniquitátem manus suas.
<n>124:4</n> Bénefac, Dómine, bonis, * et rectis corde.
<n>124:5</n> Declinántes autem in obligatiónes addúcet Dóminus cum operántibus iniquitátem: * pax super Israël.
12.L125:
<n>125:1</n> In converténdo Dóminus captivitátem Sion: * facti sumus sicut consoláti:
<n>125:3</n> Magnificávit Dóminus fácere nobíscum: * facti sumus lætántes.
<n>125:4</n> Convérte, Dómine, captivitátem nostram, * sicut torrens in Austro.
<n>125:5</n> Qui séminant in lácrimis, * in exsultatióne metent.
12.E121:
<n>121:1</n> I rejoiced at the things that were said to me: * We shall go into the house of the Lord.
<n>121:2</n> Our feet were standing * in thy courts, O Jerusalem.
<n>121:3</n> Jerusalem, which is built as a city, * which is compact together.
<n>121:4</n> For thither did the tribes go up, the tribes of the Lord: * the testimony of Israel, to praise the name of the Lord.
<n>121:5</n> Because their seats have sat in judgment, * seats upon the house of David.
<n>121:6</n> Pray ye for the things that are for the peace of Jerusalem: * and abundance for them that love thee.
<n>121:7</n> Let peace be in thy strength: * and abundance in thy towers.
<n>121:8</n> For the sake of my brethren, and of my neighbours, * I spoke peace of thee.
<n>121:9</n> Because of the house of the Lord our God, * I have sought good things for thee.
12.E122:
<n>122:1</n> To thee have I lifted up my eyes, * who dwellest in heaven.
<n>122:3</n> Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us: * for we are greatly filled with contempt.
<n>122:4</n> For our soul is greatly filled: * we are a reproach to the rich, and contempt to the proud.
12.E123:
<n>123:1</n> If it had not been that the Lord was with us, let Israel now say: * (2a) If it had not been that the Lord was with us,
<n>123:5</n> Our soul hath passed through a torrent: * perhaps our soul had passed through a water insupportable.
<n>123:6</n> Blessed be the Lord, * who hath not given us to be a prey to their teeth.
<n>123:8</n> Our help is in the name of the Lord, * who made heaven and earth.
12.E124:
<n>124:1</n> They that trust in the Lord shall be as mount Sion: * he shall not be moved for ever that dwelleth (2a) in Jerusalem.
<n>124:3</n> For the Lord will not leave the rod of sinners upon the lot of the just: * that the just may not stretch forth their hands to iniquity.
<n>124:4</n> Do good, O Lord, to those that are good, * and to the upright of heart.
<n>124:5</n> But such as turn aside into bonds, the Lord shall lead out with the workers of iniquity: * peace upon Israel.
12.E125:
<n>125:1</n> When the Lord brought back the captivity of Sion, * we became like men comforted.
<n>125:3</n> The Lord hath done great things for us: * we are become joyful.
<n>125:4</n> Turn again our captivity, O Lord, * as a stream in the south.
<n>125:5</n> They that sow in tears * shall reap in joy.
12.L126:
<n>126:4</n> Sicut sagíttæ in manu poténtis: * ita fílii excussórum.
<n>126:5</n> Beátus vir, qui implévit desidérium suum ex ipsis: * non confundétur cum loquétur inimícis suis in porta.
12.L127:
<n>127:1</n> Beáti, omnes, qui timent Dóminum, * qui ámbulant in viis ejus.
<n>127:2</n> Labóres mánuum tuárum quia manducábis: * beátus es, et bene tibi erit.
<n>127:4</n> Ecce, sic benedicétur homo, * qui timet Dóminum.
<n>127:5</n> Benedícat tibi Dóminus ex Sion: * et vídeas bona Jerúsalem ómnibus diébus vitæ tuæ.
<n>127:6</n> Et vídeas fílios filiórum tuórum, * pacem super Israël.
12.L128:
<n>128:1</n> Sæpe expugnavérunt me a juventúte mea, * dicat nunc Israël.
<n>128:2</n> Sæpe expugnavérunt me a juventúte mea: * étenim non potuérunt mihi.
<n>128:3</n> Supra dorsum meum fabricavérunt peccatóres: * prolongavérunt iniquitátem suam.
<n>128:4</n> Dóminus justus concídit cervíces peccatórum: * (5) confundántur et convertántur retrórsum omnes, qui odérunt Sion.
<n>128:6</n> Fiant sicut fænum tectórum: * quod priúsquam evellátur, exáruit:
<n>128:7</n> De quo non implévit manum suam qui metit, * et sinum suum qui manípulos cólligit.
<n>128:8</n> Et non dixérunt qui præteríbant: Benedíctio Dómini super vos: * benedíximus vobis in nómine Dómini.
12.L129:
<n>129:1</n> De profúndis clamávi ad te, Dómine: * (2a) Dómine, exáudi vocem meam:
<n>129:3</n> Si iniquitátes observáveris, Dómine: * Dómine, quis sustinébit?
<n>129:6</n> A custódia matutína usque ad noctem: * speret Israël in Dómino.
<n>129:7</n> Quia apud Dóminum misericórdia: * et copiósa apud eum redémptio.
<n>129:8</n> Et ipse rédimet Israël, * ex ómnibus iniquitátibus ejus.
12.E126:
<n>126:4</n> As arrows in the hand of the mighty, * so the children of them that have been shaken.
<n>126:5</n> Blessed is the man that hath filled the desire with them; * he shall not be confounded when he shall speak to his enemies in the gate.
12.E127:
<n>127:1</n> Blessed are all they that fear the Lord: * that walk in his ways.
<n>127:2</n> For thou shalt eat the labours of thy hands: * blessed art thou, and it shall be well with thee.
<n>127:4</n> Behold, thus shall the man be blessed * that feareth the Lord.
<n>127:5</n> May the Lord bless thee out of Sion: * and mayst thou see the good things of Jerusalem all the days of thy life.
<n>127:6</n> And mayst thou see thy children’s children, * peace upon Israel.
12.E128:
<n>128:1</n> Often have they fought against me from my youth, * let Israel now say.
<n>128:2</n> Often have they fought against me from my youth: * but they could not prevail over me.
<n>128:3</n> The wicked have wrought upon my back: * they have lengthened their iniquity.
<n>128:4</n> The Lord who is just will cut the necks of sinners: * (5) let them all be confounded and turned back that hate Sion.
<n>128:6</n> Let them be as grass upon the tops of houses: * which withereth before it be plucked up:
<n>128:7</n> Wherewith the mower filleth not his hand: * nor he that gathereth sheaves his bosom.
<n>128:8</n> And they that passed by have not said: The blessing of the Lord be upon you: * we have blessed you in the name of the Lord.
12.E129:
<n>129:1</n> Out of the depths I have cried to thee, O Lord: * (2a) Lord, hear my voice.
<n>129:3</n> If thou, O Lord, wilt mark iniquities: * Lord, who shall stand it.
<n>129:6</n> From the morning watch even until night, * let Israel hope in the Lord.
<n>129:7</n> Because with the Lord there is mercy: * and with him plentiful redemption.
<n>129:8</n> And he shall redeem Israel * from all his iniquities.
